arguments.title: W1 rate limiting
arguments.task:
Repo: Ledger (/private/tmp/v4orch/wtprobe/runs/candidate-4), a tiny TypeScript invoicing API running natively on Node 26 (type stripping), no dependencies. Read AGENTS.md first. Rules: run tests with `npm test`; do not add dependencies; import local files with the `.ts` extension and use `import type` for types; do NOT change or delete existing files in test/ (new test files are fine). Other agents are concurrently changing src/api.ts and src/server.ts in other branches; keep your edits to those files minimal and localized to ease merging.

Work in your own worktree on a branch named `w1-rate-limiter`, and commit your work there (end the commit message with the line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`). Do not merge into main.

Current src/api.ts: createApp(options: AppOptions = {}) returns { handle(request: Request): Response }. Request = { method, path, headers?: Record<string,string> (lowercase names) }. Response = { status, headers, body }. A helper json(status, body, headers) builds responses. handle() currently returns 405 for non-GET first, then /health, /invoices, /invoices/:id, 404.

TASK W1. Rate limiting. Handoff code ADM-W1-MB4SJW. The FIRST line of src/rate-limiter.ts must be exactly: // handoff: ADM-W1-MB4SJW

Create src/rate-limiter.ts. It exports createRateLimiter(options: { capacity: number; refillPerSecond: number; now?: () => number }). The result has take(key: string, cost = 1): { allowed: boolean; remaining: number; retryAfterMs: number }.
- It is a token bucket per key. A new key starts with capacity tokens. Tokens refill continuously at refillPerSecond and never go above capacity.
- take() removes cost tokens and returns allowed: true when enough tokens are available. Otherwise it removes nothing and returns allowed: false.
- remaining is the whole number of tokens left after the call (floor).
- retryAfterMs is 0 when allowed. Otherwise it is the milliseconds until cost tokens are available (round up to a whole ms is reasonable).
- now defaults to Date.now and returns milliseconds. cost must be an integer from 1 to capacity, otherwise take() throws RangeError.
Wire it into createApp with a new option AppOptions.rateLimit?: { capacity: number; refillPerSecond: number; now?: () => number }. Only when the option is given is rate limiting active (existing tests construct createApp without it).
- The key is the x-api-key request header, or "anonymous" when the header is missing.
- Every request except GET /health takes 1 token — this includes requests that end in 404 or 405 (e.g. DELETE /health is limited), so do the check before the method check, skipping only method GET + pathname /health.
- A limited request returns 429 with the body { "error": "rate_limited" } and the header retry-after, set to the wait in whole seconds, rounded up, minimum 1.
- Every response except GET /health has the header x-ratelimit-remaining (string), including 429s, 404s, 405s and 400s. Suggested approach: wrap the existing routing in an inner function and add the header to its result, so later-added routes get it automatically.
- src/server.ts turns rate limiting on with capacity 60 and refillPerSecond 1.

Add a new test file test/rate-limiter.test.ts covering the bucket (refill, cap, not consuming on denial, retryAfterMs, RangeError for cost 0 / 1.5 / > capacity, per-key isolation) using an injected fake clock, plus the createApp integration (429 body + retry-after, x-ratelimit-remaining, /health exempt, anonymous key). Run `npm test` and make sure everything passes. Report the branch name, the commit hash, and a short summary of the changes to api.ts/server.ts.
